card.title: You Know the System
card.instruction: Use another person’s knowledge of the routine while pretending you could manage perfectly well alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're opening the allotment shed. Which key do you usually use? I have my own method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The red one. Lift the handle first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I lift first too. Which way do you turn it afterwards? Comparing methods.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Left. Here, I'll open it; we need the watering cans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Go ahead. I'll check your sequence against mine. Slowly, though.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 key question claims own method; A3 asks turning direction as comparison; A5 watches B open under a checking pretext.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 key/handle advice prompts A3 direction question; B4 offers to open; A5 permits a slow demonstration as evaluation.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 offer practical steps and help because watering cans are needed.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 takeover to obtain the full routine while preserving A's supposed independent method.

specificity.evidence: A1 shed and B4 watering cans make the required access concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 slowly though exposes the need to learn beneath the claim to check sequence.
